title: Muraja'ah: 'Abasa 1 to 24 with makharij in recitation: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y7 lesson 17 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Muraja'ah rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 17. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Pace for precision
points: Breathe at the end of an ayah
Never stop in the middle of a word

panels.title: Partner makharij check
points: Ticks each of the five letters

keywords.def: revision of what is already memorised
the exit point of a letter (plural makharij, مخارج)

questions.q: Recite 80:17 to 20 at a steady pace and name any makhraj you had to slow down for.
questions.a: Pupil names e.g. ق in قُتِلَ, ث in ثُمَّ, ف in فَقَدَّرَهُۥ.
At the end of an ayah
options: At the end of an ayah
In the middle of a word

questions.q: Breakout pairs: recite 80:1 to 24 to a partner who ticks the five letters on the pupil PDF. Today's rota group recites 80:17 to 24 to the teacher.
questions.a: Partner sheet with ticks for ع ح ض ذ ث and one target; teacher records rota scores.

questions.q: Stretch: record yourself at home reciting 80:1 to 24 and note one makhraj to improve.
questions.a: A written note in the portal log naming one letter and ayah.
A) at a steady, measured pace. Tartil (73:4) is measured recitation, giving every letter its right.

questions.q: Which letter must not become ه?
Think again: Is it harder to say a letter correctly on its own or in the middle of fast recitation? Why?
questions.a: In recitation: we focus on memory and flow. Steady pace (tartil) gives time for each letter.
